I've been farming this land for 55 years. I know this soil. My father farmed it before me. The wheat goes in come October, the maize follows after the harvest in June — same 2 mu, same as always. My legs aren't what they were, and there's only me and my wife, so I can't do anything too complicated or too heavy. The well has been reliable. I'll manage.

For the wheat, I put it in after the autumn rains settle. I use the improved seeds from the village supply station — I stopped saving my own seed years ago because the new ones give better grain. I spread the base fertilizer before plowing, then top-dress at jointing. Three waterings: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. I spray for aphids in spring, maybe once more if the rust comes. I plough deep in autumn — that's always been my way, keeps the soil loose.

For the maize, I plant right after the wheat comes off, no time to waste. Hybrid seed, everyone uses it now. I do rotary tillage — I'm too old to plough again so soon. The well handles two or three waterings through the dry July. I put nitrogen down twice, at planting and when it tassels. One spray for corn borer, maybe a second if it gets bad.

Two mu, two crops, two seasons. That's the whole year.
